article_lead.description: the trace of a smoothing fit's response-influence matrix, measuring how much flexibility remains after penalisation so curves can be compared with ordinary regression fits

efron2004_prediction_error.title: The Estimation of Prediction Error: Covariance Penalties and Cross-Validation
efron2004_prediction_error.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

shared_changes.change: In the paragraph beginning ‘Putting a knot at every x_i’ (around line 30), replace the claims that edf is a polynomial degree, that a full straight-line fit has one edf, and that a reduced basis necessarily interpolates when lambda tends to zero. State that edf is trace of the response influence matrix, a cubic spline's full intercept-plus-slope null space has two edf (a centred smooth term has one), and interpolation at zero penalty needs a full-rank basis spanning the observed responses. Keep all substantive knot/cross-validation discussion and citations, verify claims against the new effective-degrees-of-freedom page, and rebuild the notes and dependent articles.

At the kyphosis discussion around line 54, the statements comparing edf 2.22 to quadratic and cubic polynomial degrees are only an informal complexity analogy. Reword to an influence-matrix flexibility interpretation without removing the fitted edf, shape, intercept, chi-square or p-value. Rebuild dependent notes and articles.
